memory-owner-pooled-lifetime.title: Manage pooled memory lifetime with IMemoryOwner
memory-owner-pooled-lifetime.short: Tie rented Memory lifetime to an explicit disposable owner
memory-owner-pooled-lifetime.summary: IMemoryOwner<T> represents both rented Memory<T> and the responsibility to return or release it.
memory-owner-pooled-lifetime.why: Ownership stays explicit even when Memory is passed across asynchronous operations.
memory-owner-pooled-lifetime.tips: Never retain the Memory after disposing its owner, and slice it to the actual logical length before use.

utf8jsonreader-zero-copy-values.title: Read Utf8JsonReader values without unnecessary strings
utf8jsonreader-zero-copy-values.short: Consume ValueSpan or ValueSequence directly when appropriate
utf8jsonreader-zero-copy-values.summary: Utf8JsonReader can expose JSON values over the input UTF-8 buffer instead of allocating a string for every token.
utf8jsonreader-zero-copy-values.why: Direct parsing can reduce temporary allocations and GC pressure when scanning large JSON payloads.
utf8jsonreader-zero-copy-values.tips: Check HasValueSequence and never retain spans beyond the lifetime of the underlying input buffer.

httpclient-automatic-decompression.title: Automatically decompress HttpClient responses
httpclient-automatic-decompression.short: Configure gzip and Brotli decoding on SocketsHttpHandler
httpclient-automatic-decompression.summary: AutomaticDecompression lets the HTTP handler decode supported Content-Encoding responses before callers read the body.
httpclient-automatic-decompression.why: It preserves compressed network transfer without duplicating decompression code at every call site.
httpclient-automatic-decompression.tips: Combine it with correct HttpClient lifetime management, and leave it disabled when the application needs the original compressed bytes.

assemblyloadcontext-resolving-fallback.title: Add fallback dependency resolution to AssemblyLoadContext
assemblyloadcontext-resolving-fallback.short: Resolve dependencies that normal assembly probing could not find
assemblyloadcontext-resolving-fallback.summary: AssemblyLoadContext.Resolving is a fallback hook for supplying assemblies that the normal load process could not resolve.
assemblyloadcontext-resolving-fallback.why: It supports plugin-specific dependency layouts without mixing custom probing into unrelated application code.
assemblyloadcontext-resolving-fallback.tips: Avoid unbounded or recursive probing and prefer well-defined plugin boundaries plus AssemblyDependencyResolver results.

task-unobserved-exception-last-resort.title: Treat UnobservedTaskException as a last-resort diagnostic
task-unobserved-exception-last-resort.short: Detect abandoned Task failures without using the event as normal error handling
task-unobserved-exception-last-resort.summary: TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException reports Task exceptions that remained unobserved until finalization-related processing.
task-unobserved-exception-last-resort.why: It can reveal broken fire-and-forget paths, but its timing is unsuitable for ordinary control flow.
task-unobserved-exception-last-resort.tips: Await tasks and handle failures where work is launched; use this event only as a diagnostic safety net.

memorycache-stampede-singleflight.title: Prevent cache stampedes with single-flight loading
memorycache-stampede-singleflight.short: Coalesce concurrent misses for the same expensive value
memorycache-stampede-singleflight.summary: When many requests miss the same cache entry together, they can all perform the same expensive regeneration concurrently.
memorycache-stampede-singleflight.why: Duplicate loads can overwhelm a database or remote service even though a cache is present.
memorycache-stampede-singleflight.tips: Coordinate per key or use a single-flight design while preserving parallelism between unrelated keys and releasing gates on failures.

arraysegment-legacy-buffer-slice.title: Use ArraySegment for legacy array slices
arraysegment-legacy-buffer-slice.short: Represent an array offset and count without copying
arraysegment-legacy-buffer-slice.summary: ArraySegment<T> describes a portion of an array and remains useful at API boundaries that predate Span<T> and Memory<T>.
arraysegment-legacy-buffer-slice.why: It avoids copying an entire buffer when an existing API accepts ArraySegment values.
arraysegment-legacy-buffer-slice.tips: For newer APIs also consider Span or Memory, and remember that the underlying array remains shared and mutable.

timeprovider-deterministic-tests.title: Make time-dependent tests deterministic with TimeProvider
timeprovider-deterministic-tests.short: Advance a fake clock instead of waiting for wall-clock time
timeprovider-deterministic-tests.summary: Code designed around TimeProvider can inject a test clock so delays and deadlines are controlled independently of real time.
timeprovider-deterministic-tests.why: Slow and flaky tests that wait seconds or minutes can become fast and repeatable.
timeprovider-deterministic-tests.tips: Do not mix direct DateTime.Now calls into the same logic; route both time reads and supported delays through the abstraction.

rate-limiter-partition-cardinality.title: Bound PartitionedRateLimiter key cardinality
rate-limiter-partition-cardinality.short: Do not create limiter partitions directly from unlimited user input
rate-limiter-partition-cardinality.summary: Using arbitrary input as a partition key can create large numbers of short-lived limiter states.
rate-limiter-partition-cardinality.why: A rate limiter can otherwise become a memory-pressure target under high-cardinality or hostile input.
rate-limiter-partition-cardinality.tips: Normalize to managed tenant or identity keys and map unknown or anonymous callers into a bounded partition strategy.

system-io-hashing-noncryptographic.title: Use System.IO.Hashing for non-cryptographic hashing
system-io-hashing-noncryptographic.short: Separate fast checksums from security-sensitive hashing
system-io-hashing-noncryptographic.summary: System.IO.Hashing provides fast algorithms such as XxHash for checksums, lookup, and other non-cryptographic workloads.
system-io-hashing-noncryptographic.why: It offers a lightweight option when resistance to adversarial manipulation is not required.
system-io-hashing-noncryptographic.tips: Use appropriate cryptographic primitives such as SHA-family hashes when authenticity, signatures, passwords, or hostile inputs are involved.
